looks_bad_but_fine.why: 290-entry hardcoded map scores as a hotspot and is depended on by store, which could look like an unstable god-file many components rely on, but it has exactly one consumer (internal/store/store.go) and the map's values are identical to the function's own fallback pattern 'data/'+name+'.json', so there is no fan-out coupling risk despite the size.

main.go imports five internal packages (build, dispatch, flags, httpc, store), which looks like a coupled hub, but this is the composition root of a single small binary, not a shared library being fanned out to multiple consumers, so high import count here is expected.

not_assessed: No import-cycle tooling, ADR, or boundary/layer contract exists in the repo (no docs beyond README.md and docs/runbook.md, no lint config for import boundaries), so 'intended layering' could only be inferred from directory names, not verified against a stated policy.

internal/crypto and internal/shell are not imported by any other file in the repository; whether this reflects deliberate scaffolding, in-progress work, or true dead code cannot be determined from repository contents alone and is a dead-code/design question outside the cycle/coupling scope of this architecture pass.
